candidate.scope: Rust module and function declarations, local mod/use imports and calls, literal reqwest/client HTTP origins, and literal sqlx table reads and writes.
candidate.unsupportedBoundary: Traits, macros, generics, ownership semantics, compiler resolution, runtime behavior, dynamic HTTP destinations, and dynamic SQL remain explicit unsupported or deferred behavior.

thresholds.graduateImpact: A missed conformance case blocks graduation.
The bounded pilot must cover at least four of five predeclared semantic families.
A higher unknown rate requires a narrower support claim.
Precision below the floor blocks graduation.
Recall below the floor blocks graduation.
A bounded fixture above 500 ms requires a performance review before graduation.
A projected maintenance cost above eight hours per quarter requires a capacity decision.

thresholds.unit: independent adopter or maintainer demand signals
thresholds.graduateImpact: Graduation requires at least one independently recorded demand signal.

thresholds.unit: named primary and backup security owners
thresholds.graduateImpact: Missing primary or backup ownership blocks any promotion.
Incomplete evidence blocks promotion and release.

measurements.notes: The Rust bounded case passed both conformance repetitions with stable output and complete evidence.
Four bounded families are covered: modules, calls, literal HTTP, and literal SQL; compiler-sensitive Rust semantics remain outside the pilot.
Two dynamic constructs are explicit unsupported diagnostics across six bounded probes; no unsupported relationship is silently guessed.
The pilot predicted nine supported edges and all nine matched the expected set.
All nine expected supported edges were recovered in the bounded corpus.
The latest local compatibility replay observed 3.586 ms for the Rust bounded case; this is a fixture budget, not a universal throughput claim.
The bounded pilot has one named owner, one backup, a quarterly review cadence, and a six-hour quarterly maintenance estimate.

measurements.unit: independent adopter or maintainer demand signals
measurements.notes: No independent demand signal is recorded in the local evidence set; the gate therefore refuses a broad expansion commitment.

measurements.unit: named primary and backup security owners
measurements.notes: The matrix and lifecycle policy name extractor-maintainers as primary and core-maintainers as backup, with private intake and archive rules.
Every emitted pilot edge or diagnostic has source-bound evidence or an explicit unsupported reason.

decision.rationale: Retain the bounded Rust pilot as an implemented, explicitly scoped experiment. Conformance, precision, recall, evidence, security ownership, and the local performance budget pass; the semantic boundary is narrow and no independent demand signal is recorded. Broad Rust language support remains deferred and no new implementation commitment is authorized.
rejectedAlternatives: graduate — rejected because the gate has no independent demand signal and compiler-sensitive Rust semantics remain outside the pilot.
narrow — rejected because the declared bounded slice meets its quality and safety floors.
retire — rejected because the bounded pilot is reproducible, accurate, owned, and useful as a language-neutral compatibility experiment.
decision.supportBoundary: Keep cartograph.rust limited to the declared module/function, local import/call, literal HTTP, and literal SQL slice. Keep language.rust deferred; do not add traits, macros, generics, ownership, compiler-resolution, runtime, or dynamic-query coverage under this gate.
